entries.title: Matthew 6:1
segments: To be seen of them. Jesus here implies the worthlessness of human praise, apart from the righteousness approved by God.

entries.title: Matthew 6:2
segments: They have received their reward. The acts done to earn the applause of men have no reward beyond that.

entries.title: Matthew 6:5
segments: Hypocrites. From a Greek word meaning the acting of a part on the stage; hence pretenders, deceivers.

entries.title: Matthew 6:6
segments: Pray to thy Father who is in secret. Our Lord here contrasts the praying hypocrite with the sincere believer.  He does not say that secret prayer as such is better than public prayer; but commands his hearers to shun the habits of those whose prayers in public are no better than mockery.  It is not a question of place.  Sincerity is the test, whether prayer is public or private.

entries.title: Matthew 6:7
segments: Vain repetitions. 'Vain' because the mere sound of pious words is thought to have some merit.

entries.title: Matthew 6:9
segments:
Our Father. The fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man are taught in these two words.
 

 
Hallowed be thy name. Reverence for the name of God must precede any petition to Him.

entries.title: Matthew 6:10
segments:
Thy kingdom come. The Jews were always looking for a kingdom.  This expectant habit of the Jewish mind is here recognized, but what is meant is the spiritual kingdom in which righteousness and truth shall prevail.
 

 
Thy will be done. A prayer that faith in God may be realized in entire submission to Him.

entries.title: Matthew 6:11
segments: Daily bread. But the daily needs of the body may not be met without foresight and work by him who prays.  The truth taught is the need of daily conscious dependence upon God.

entries.title: Matthew 6:12
segments: As we also have forgiven. Our debts, or sins, will not be forgiven us by God unless we are forgiving.  All through this prayer it is taken for granted that we cannot ask for ourselves what we deny to others.

entries.title: Matthew 6:13
segments: Bring us not into temptation. When God permits temptation, He provides a way of escape.

entries.title: Matthew 6:16
segments: As the hypocrites, of a sad countenance. Here the warning to the insincere is repeated.  It is not the manner of fasting which counts, but the motive, which prompts it.

entries.title: Matthew 6:19
segments: Moth and rust. In the East a large part of riches consisted in costly garments especially liable to destruction by moths.

entries.title: Matthew 6:21
segments: There will thy heart be also. One whose treasures are his earthly hopes and desires will have a heart for nothing else.  One whose mind is centered on holiness of life, will be molded in the image of the Master.

entries.title: Matthew 6:24
segments: No man can serve two masters. This and

illustrate the need of singleness, that is, whole-hearted devotion, in the service of god.  As a diseased eye admits no light or at least an imperfect light to the body, so a diseased conscience, 'the light that is in thee,' darkens or blinds the soul.  No man can serve both God and the world.
 

 
Mammon. Riches.

entries.title: Matthew 6:25
segments: Be not anxious. A reproof of believers who worry.

entries.title: Matthew 6:27
segments: One cubit. A foot and a half.  Here it is used figuratively and may be taken to mean any arbitrary amount or measure.

entries.title: Matthew 6:28
segments: Consider the lilies. Think of their beauty and how perfectly they have been clothed, although not troubled or anxious about their raiment.

entries.title: Matthew 6:30
segments: Cast into the oven. In the East dried grass is often burned to heat the ovens of baked clay.

entries.title: Matthew 6:32
segments: Your heavenly Father knoweth. A fact sufficient to remove from believers all anxiety about bodily needs.

entries.title: Matthew 6:33
segments: Seek ye first his kingdom, and his righteousness. Having sought and found this kingdom, which is within us, all lesser blessings follow.

entries.title: Matthew 6:34
segments: Be not therefore anxious. The Master's disciples are to be cheerful and confident.  Christianity has too often been thought of as a religion of sadness.  Among the most precious words of Jesus are these: 'Be of good cheer; I have over come the world.'
